content_sections.body: Start with the model: 'On Saturday I bought tomatoes and asked the seller for a bag.' Replace one detail with your own information about a Saturday market visit. Then add a short follow-up or reason. This builds the skill to use a short frame to report what happened and when.
content_sections.title: Build a useful turn (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about a Saturday market visit. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Use a short frame to report what happened and when.
content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Create a short message about a Saturday market visit without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.
content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)

exercises.correct_answer: On Saturday I bought tomatoes and asked the seller for a bag.
options: On Saturday I bought tomatoes and asked the seller for a bag.
My card did not work at the machine, so I asked a staff member for help.
I can choose language for stories, requests, and everyday problems.
exercises.prompt: Choose the response that gives a clear, useful message for this situation: a Saturday market visit.
Complete the model with the missing words: 'On Saturday I bought tomatoes and asked the seller ____.'
Read this short message for the lesson 'Event-reporting chunks' and identify the real-life situation it describes.

acceptable_answers: The message is about a Saturday market visit.
questions.question: What situation does the message describe?

exercises.stimulus: On Saturday I bought tomatoes and asked the seller for a bag. The message gives one main point and one detail for the listener.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 30–45 seconds about a Saturday market visit. State the main message, add a relevant detail, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Communicates the main message about a Saturday market visit clearly.
Adds a relevant detail and responds appropriately to a follow-up question.

language_focus: Use a short frame to report what happened and when.
objectives: Use a short frame to report what happened and when.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about a Saturday market visit.

listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns a Saturday market visit.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about a Saturday market visit.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about a Saturday market visit. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?
listening.transcript: On Saturday I bought tomatoes and asked the seller for a bag.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in a Saturday market visit easy to hear.
pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for a Saturday market visit in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in event-reporting chunks

constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about a Saturday market visit.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay a Saturday market visit. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about a Saturday market visit.
writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about a Saturday market visit. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.

title: Event-reporting chunks
